name: Jaroah
overview: Jaroah is a male figure from the tribe of Gad, identified specifically as the son of Gilead. His mention in Scripture is concise, emphasizing his lineage within the Gadite people. There are no additional notes on his life or actions beyond his tribal and familial identity.
namesAndTitles: The name Jaroah means 'soft, delicate,' which is a proper name recorded in 1 Chronicles 5:14. There is no indication that this name was given directly by God, but it reflects a personal designation within the biblical record.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Jaroah as the son of Gilead and infers Huri as his father, establishing a clear paternal lineage. Beyond these relationships, no further family connections are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Jaroah's significance lies primarily in his genealogical placement within the tribe of Gad, serving as a link in the ancestral line of this Israelite tribe. His mention in 1 Chronicles 5:14 helps preserve the historical record of the Gadites and their descendants, contributing to the broader biblical narrative of Israel's tribal heritage.
